statuses.verified: Cross-checked against the official portal within the review cycle.
statuses.pending_review: Record exists but a re-check against the official source is due.
statuses.stale: Last verification older than the review cycle — treat with caution.

policy.amounts_disclaimer: Benefit amounts are indicative of recent public cycles and must be re-verified on the official portal before applying.

policy.deadline_policy: A deadline in the past is recorded as-is rather than replaced with a guess at the next cycle. agents/verify_dataset.py flags it as deadline_stale, which is the intended signal that the record needs re-verification when the next annual window opens. An honest past date tells a student to prepare for next June; an invented future date sends them to a form that does not exist.
policy.confidence_policy: verified = a recent, scheme-specific source confirms the current date and portal. pending_review = sources conflict, the department has published nothing for 2026-27, or the date is carried forward from the previous cycle. Records are never upgraded to verified on the strength of an aggregator repeating another aggregator.

retired.reason: Merged. UGC's own FAQ on the NSP portal states that the National Scholarship for Post Graduate Studies (NSPGS) is 'an umbrella scheme by merging four different scholarship schemes for postgraduate studies i.e. (i) PG Indira Gandhi single girl child scholarship, (ii) PG scholarship for university rank holders, (iii) PG scholarship for SC/ST students pursuing professional courses and (iv) Post Graduate Scholarship for GATE/GPAT'. Single girl child is now a preference within the 30% women reservation under NSPGS, not a separate scheme.

Merged into the National Scholarship for Post Graduate Studies (NSPGS) along with the single-girl-child, SC/ST professional and GATE/GPAT PG schemes. NSPGS selects purely on all-India merit for 10,000 slots a year; university rank is no longer a separate award.

No application window has been open since October 2024 — two full cycles missed. DST told the Rajya Sabha on 13 August 2026 that INSPIRE (SHE) is under REDESIGN and has not been discontinued, but no form, deadline or eligibility has been published. The dataset previously carried a deadline of 2026-10-15, which would have told a student to apply for a scheme with no open application at all. Re-add when DST publishes a notice; the expected window is around January 2027 based on the previous cycle.
